lessons.title: Value vs Reference Types

quickCheck.prompt: Which is a value type in Swift?
quickCheck.explanation: Structs are value types — they are copied on assignment, giving each variable an independent instance. Classes are reference types that share identity.

lessons.title: Optionals & Unwrapping

quickCheck.prompt: What does `nil ?? 42` evaluate to when the left side is nil?
quickCheck.explanation: The nil-coalescing operator returns the right-hand side when the left is nil, providing a default value without force unwrapping.

lessons.title: Protocols & Generics

quickCheck.prompt: What keyword provides a default implementation for a protocol method?
quickCheck.explanation: Default implementations are added via `extension` on the protocol — conforming types inherit the default but can override it with their own implementation.

questions.prompt: What is the default access level in Swift?
questions.explanation: Declarations are `internal` by default — visible within the module but not outside.
Arrays are value types using copy-on-write, so `b` is an independent copy; appending to `b` doesn't affect `a`.

codeSnippet.code:
var a = [1, 2]
var b = a
b.append(3)
print(a)

questions.prompt: What does optional chaining return when any link is nil?
questions.explanation: Optional chaining short-circuits to nil if any step in the chain is nil, safely returning an Optional of the final expression's type.

questions.prompt: In a closure, capturing `self` with `[weak self]` means…
questions.explanation: Capturing `[weak self]` makes self optional inside the closure, breaking a potential retain cycle between the closure and the owning object.
